feedback: If a learner stalls or confuses inches and feet, treat it as lack of exposure, not a misconception: scaffold with real objects and referents, then re-ask.
Reinforce that within-imperial facts (12 inches = 1 foot) are exact, unlike the cross-system facts that use rounded conversion factors.
activities.intendedInsight: Imperial units are often unfamiliar; knowing the names, what they measure, and the exact relationships within imperial supports confident estimation without a false belief getting in the way.
learnerActions: Meet and say the imperial unit names: inch, foot, pound, ounce, stone, pint, gallon.
Match each unit to what it measures (length, mass or capacity) and to a familiar referent (an adult's thumb-width ≈ 1 inch; foot-long ruler = 12 inches).
Learn the exact within-imperial relationships (1 foot = 12 inches; 16 ounces = 1 pound) and contrast them with the approximate cross-system facts.
Re-attempt an estimation question after building familiarity.
activities.title: Imperial vocabulary familiarisation
